question: According to his ancient biographer, what turned the merchant Zeno of Citium, founder of Stoicism, to philosophy?
answer: A shipwreck. Diogenes Laertius says Zeno lost a cargo of purple dye near Piraeus, walked up to Athens and sat reading Xenophon's memoir of Socrates in a bookshop. He asked where such men could be found; the bookseller pointed to the Cynic Crates, passing by. Zeno later said his voyage prospered when he was wrecked.
move: Judge a disaster only after you have seen which door it opened.
ask: What disaster of mine turned out to open a door I would never have chosen?
reference: Diogenes Laertius, Lives of Eminent Philosophers VII.2-5, trans. Hicks, Loeb Classical Library, Harvard University Press, 1925
